n: David describes the inner voice of a wicked person: sin speaks to him like an oracle, and he has no reverence for God at all. Paul quotes this line in Romans.

f.w: there is no fear of God before his eyes

n: The wicked man flatters himself, thinking his sin will never be discovered or hated — self-deception at its worst.

f.w: flattereth himself in his own eyes

n: His words are full of wrong and deceit, and he has stopped trying to be wise or do good.
Even lying in bed he plots harm. He chooses a bad path on purpose and never rejects evil.

f.w: He deviseth mischief upon his bed

n: Suddenly the psalm lifts its eyes: God’s loyal love is as high as the heavens, his faithfulness reaches the clouds. The contrast with the wicked could not be sharper.

f.w: Thy mercy, O LORD, is in the heavens

n: God’s righteousness stands like massive mountains, and his judgments go as deep as the ocean. He cares for both humans and animals.

f.g: The vast ocean depths — beyond human measuring.

n: God’s loyal love is precious, so people take refuge under his wings like chicks under a mother bird — or under the cherubim’s wings over the ark.
Those who come to God feast at a rich banquet in his house and drink from a river of delights.

f.g: “Pleasures” is Hebrew ʿedenim, related to Eden — a river of delights.

n: God is the source of life itself, and only by his light can we see truly. Latter-day revelation teaches that the light of Christ fills all things and gives life.

f.w: in thy light shall we see light

n: David asks God to keep showing his loyal love to those who know him and his justice to the honest-hearted.

f.g: Knowing God in Hebrew implies a close, covenant relationship.

n: He asks protection from proud people who would trample him and wicked hands that would drive him away.

f.g: The arrogant who would stamp on him.

n: As if seeing it already happen, David points: there the evildoers lie fallen, thrown down and unable to rise.

f.g: As if pointing to the very spot where they fall.
